1. Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production

Source: HackerNews | Topic: hn | Coverage: 1 source | Discussion

Summary

Tesla is reportedly winding down production of the Cybertruck due to poor sales performance. The decision follows years of market challenges and shifting consumer demand for the vehicle. Production is expected to be fully phased out over the coming years.

My Take

It turns out that building a stainless steel refrigerator on wheels that looks like it was rendered on a PlayStation 1 wasn't the masterstroke everyone thought it was. It's the ultimate lesson in hubris: just because you can design a car in a CAD program doesn't mean it belongs on a public road. 2. Libghostty 1.0

4. A Jev that can ask Opus for help gives Opus accuracy at 4x lower cost

Source: HackerNews | Topic: hn | Coverage: 1 source | Discussion

Summary

A new method using a smaller 'judge' model to query a more powerful model like Opus has demonstrated significant cost savings while maintaining accuracy. By offloading simpler tasks to the judge, developers can reduce their reliance on expensive high-end models. This approach optimizes API usage for complex identity resolution workflows.

My Take

We've reached the point in the AI hype cycle where we’re hiring smaller, cheaper AI interns to manage the expensive, genius-level AI managers. It’s basically corporate middle management, but for silicon. 7. US FAA says it will phase out floppy disks from air traffic control by 2028

Source: HackerNews | Topic: hn | Coverage: 1 source | Discussion

Summary

The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has announced plans to phase out the use of floppy disks in air traffic control systems by 2028. These legacy systems have been in operation for decades, maintaining stability despite the obsolescence of the storage medium. The transition to modern digital infrastructure is part of a broader modernization effort.

My Take

The FAA is finally retiring the floppy disk, which is honestly the most impressive endurance test in the history of consumer hardware. We’re out here worrying about AI taking over the world, while the planes are literally being guided by technology that was considered 'vintage' when I was in grade school. It’s comforting to know that the most critical infrastructure on Earth is held together by sheer stubbornness and magnetic plastic.
